# Pages, trees and regions

A page is a row (slug, title, status, frame, SEO) plus a tree (`splash.tree/3`) of nodes. Header, footer, above and below are regions: their trees live on pages named `region-*`, and `region.read` gives their root ids. Every node edit is a `tree.commit` of `splash.ops/2` ops.

## tree.commit

Apply an invertible batch of splash.ops/2 ops to a page tree. Each op names its node by `id` (insert names `parentId` and `index`): `insert` { parentId, index, node }, `remove` { id }, `move` { id, parentId, index }, `set_props` { id, patch } (a patch of props; null removes one), `set_style` { id, scope, patch }, `set_meta` { id, anchor?, name?, meta?, visibleTo?, locked? }, `set_attrs` { id, patch }, `set_variant` { id, variant }, `set_theme` { id, theme }, `set_mixins` { id, mixins }, `set_visibility` { id, visibility }, `set_type` { id, type }, `set_override` { id, target, patch }; only `insert` carries a whole node with its `props`. A node's section anchor is the node field `anchor`, not a prop or meta key. In a set_style patch and in the styles.sheet of an inserted node, each declaration value may be a raw CSS string ("clamp(22px, 2.3vw, 34px)", "{color.text}" for a token) or { kind: "raw", css }; the server tokenizes it with the inspector's parser and refuses a value the style catalogue does not allow, at its path. A `scope` is a scope key, `base` or segments joined by `|` in this order: `bp:<breakpoint>` (a site breakpoint, mobile-first: `bp:md` from 768 px up), `cq:(max-width:767px)` or `cq:<name>(min-width:480px)` (a container condition, the way to style a desktop-first range; a named container is an ancestor whose base `container-name` names it), `mq:(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)` (one media condition: reduced motion, colour scheme, contrast, forced colours, hover, pointer, orientation or print), `v:<variant>`, `th:<theme>`, `a:<type>[data-state="<state>"]` (the nearest ancestor of that type in a state its entry declares, such as `a:sticky-bar[data-state="scrolled"]`), `p:<part>` (a part of the node's component), `s:<state>` (pseudo-classes, at most one pseudo-element and attribute selectors on the node: `s::hover`, `s::focus-visible`, `s::has(> img)`, `s:[data-state="open"]`) and `t:<selector>` (a descendant, `t: img`, or a child, `t:> .icon`, that the value applies to). So `bp:md|s::hover|t: img` styles the node's images while the node is hovered, from 768 px up. `bp:` and `cq:` compile to container queries on the page's content box (or on the nearest node that sets `container-type`): where a page's frame scales (`responsiveMode: "scale"`, from its `scaleFromWidth`, 769 px by default), that box keeps the frame's design width, so they resolve at the design width there. A hover state applies only on a device that hovers. The class is content.edit, but only a content-prop edit (a set_props of a content field) needs no more: every other op of the batch needs site.edit.

- permission `content.edit` (admin, editor); class `transaction`; writes `tree:{pageId}`; undoable with `history.undo`.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `pageId` | string (min 1) | yes |
| `ops` | ({ op: "insert", parentId: nodeId, slot?: string, index: integer ≥0, node: { meta?: …, styles?: …, variant?: …, theme?: …, visibility?: …, attrs?: …, id: …, kind: …, type: …, children: … } \| { meta?: …, styles?: …, variant?: …, theme?: …, visibility?: …, attrs?: …, id: …, slot?: …, name?: …, anchor?: …, locked?: …, pro… (full schema: discover_operations) | yes |
| `ops[].op` | "insert" \| "set_style" \| "remove" \| "move" \| "set_props" \| "set_mixins" \| "set_variant" \| "set_theme" \| "set_visibility" \| "set_type" \| "set_meta" \| "set_attrs" \| "set_override" | yes |

Output: { revision: integer ≥0, inverse: ({ op: "insert", parentId: nodeId, slot?: string, index: integer ≥0, node: { meta?: …, styles?: …, variant?: …, theme?: …, visibility?: …, attrs?: …, id: …, kind: …, type: …, children: … } \| { meta?: …, styles?: …, variant?: …, theme?: …, visibility?: …, attrs?: …, id: …, slot?: …, name… (full schema: discover_operations)

Example input:

```json
{"pageId":"6f1d2c3b-4a59-4e8d-9c7b-1a2b3c4d5e6f","ops":[{"op":"insert","parentId":"root0000","index":0,"node":{"id":"hero0001","kind":"section","type":"section","anchor":"hero","name":"Opening section","styles":{"sheet":{"base":{"position":"sticky","top":"0","min-height":"100svh","max-width":"none","padding-inline":"0"}}},"children":[{"id":"claim001","kind":"primitive","type":"text","props":{"text":{"en-US":"Architecture for the places we live in"}},"styles":{"sheet":{"base":{"font-size":"clamp(22px, 2.3vw, 34px)","color":{"kind":"raw","css":"{color.text.accent}"}}}}}]}},{"op":"set_props","id":"claim001","patch":{"text":{"en-US":"Architecture for the places we live and work in"}}},{"op":"set_style","id":"claim001","scope":"bp:md","patch":{"margin-inline-start":"50%"}},{"op":"set_meta","id":"hero0001","anchor":"opening","name":"Opening"},{"op":"set_attrs","id":"claim001","patch":{"data-tone":"quiet"}},{"op":"set_variant","id":"button01","variant":["ghost"]},{"op":"move","id":"intro001","parentId":"hero0001","index":1},{"op":"remove","id":"old00001"}]}
```

> A text prop keeps its shape: a plain string is the same in every language; a map `{ "it": "…", "en-US": "…" }` holds one text per language. Change only the language asked.

> Style values may be tokens (`"{space.4}"`, `"{color.text.accent}"`) or raw CSS; use a token whenever one exists. Scopes are `base` and breakpoints such as `bp:md`; `null` removes a declaration.

> Inserted nodes need fresh 8-character ids (`[0-9a-z]{8}`) unique in the page. `set_props` never stores a value equal to the default (`I8.default_stored`).

> Findings in the answer cover the whole page: look at the ones whose `nodeId` you touched.

## content.importMarkdown

Replace the content of a richtext node with Markdown, in one language (the site's main one when `locale` is absent; the other languages keep theirs). It reads `#` headings at their level, paragraphs, nested lists, fenced code with its language, pipe tables (head row as header cells), `> **Note:** …` quotes as callouts (Note/Nota, Tip/Suggerimento, Warning/Pitfall/Attenzione/Avvertenza; other quotes stay quotes), `<kbd>` keys, links the rich text allows, `**bold**`, `*em*` and `code`. A picture `![alt](src)` must be in the site's media library, named `media:<id>` or by its file name; one that is not is refused (upload it first). A YAML front matter block is skipped. One undoable tree commit.

- permission `content.edit` (admin, editor); class `transaction`; writes `tree:{pageId}`; undoable with `history.undo`.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `pageId` | string (min 1) | yes |
| `nodeId` | nodeId | yes |
| `markdown` | string (max 400000) | yes |
| `locale` | string (min 2, max 35) |  |

Output: { revision: integer ≥0, inverse: ({ op: "insert", parentId: nodeId, slot?: string, index: integer ≥0, node: { meta?: …, styles?: …, variant?: …, theme?: …, visibility?: …, attrs?: …, id: …, kind: …, type: …, children: … } \| { meta?: …, styles?: …, variant?: …, theme?: …, visibility?: …, attrs?: …, id: …, slot?: …, name… (full schema: discover_operations)

Example input:

```json
{"pageId":"6f1d2c3b-4a59-4e8d-9c7b-1a2b3c4d5e6f","nodeId":"text0001","locale":"en-US","markdown":"# Build a page\n\nPress <kbd>Esc</kbd> to select the container.\n\n> **Note:** Every change saves on its own.\n\n```bash\nyarn splash context\n```\n"}
```

> Pictures must already be in the media library (`media:<id>` or the file name).

## page.create

Create a page (`slug`, `title` per locale, and optionally `slugs`, its slug in each other locale such as `{ "en": "method" }`, `frame`, the theme layout frame it renders in, `parentId`, `pageType`, SEO and members-only fields) with an empty tree. `status` defaults to draft; a draft page stays out of the site publish, so pass `status: "published"` for a page the next publication.publish should serve. Fill the tree with tree.commit in the same batch: read the new root id with tree.read through a $ref to this operation's page.id. A section's anchor is the node field `anchor` in that tree, not a page field, `meta.anchor` or `props.anchor`. A `pageType: "dynamic"` page names a collection in `collectionKey` and is the detail page of its items: it answers `/<slug>/<item slug>` in each locale, and its tree binds the item. Page validation and ownership checks apply.

- permission `site.structure` (admin, workspace owner); class `transaction`; writes `pages`; undoable with `history.undo`.

## page.update

Patch a page's fields as { pageId, patch }: slug, `slugs` names the page's slug in each other locale, as `{ "en": "method" }`: the page answers `/en/method` in English (a page under it reads `/en/method/<its English slug>`) and its `slug` in the default locale; a locale without one answers `slug`. A `slugs` value sets that locale's slug, `null` removes it, a locale left out keeps its own; no sibling page may answer the same slug in any locale. Renaming a published page (its slug, a slug per locale or its parent) adds a 301 from each old address to the new one to the site's redirects (redirects.read). Also title, `frame` (the theme layout frame it renders in, such as `default`, which reflows at the site breakpoints, or a scaled canvas such as `scale-canvas`; layout.update edits a frame), status, SEO, members-only access or `meta`. `patch.status: "published"` marks a draft page for the next site publish. `patch.meta` replaces the page's whole meta, so read the page first (page.read) and send its meta back with your change. `meta.layoutOverrides` overrides the frame for this page alone, layer by layer, where the frame's `overridePolicy` allows it: `background` ({ color, image, overlay, texture }: the page's own background colour, as raw CSS such as `var(--ds-color-bg-inverse)`), `header`, `footer`, `scroll` and `chrome`. Page validation and ownership checks apply.

- permission `site.edit` (admin, editor); class `transaction`; writes `pages`; undoable with `history.undo`.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `pageId` | string (min 1) | yes |
| `patch` | { slug?: string (min 1), slugs?: Record<string, string \| null>, title?: Record<string, string>, frame?: string, dynamic?: boolean, position?: integer ≥-9007199254740991, parentId?: string (min 1) \| null, requireAuth?: boolean, requiredRoles?: string (max 40)[] (≤50), meta?: Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| nu… (full schema: discover_operations) | yes |

Output: { page: { slug: string (min 1), slugs?: Record<string, string>, title: Record<string, string>, frame: string, dynamic: boolean, position: integer ≥-9007199254740991, parentId: string \| null, requireAuth: boolean, requiredRoles?: string (max 40)[] (≤50), meta: Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (… \| … \| …… (full schema: discover_operations)

Example input:

```json
{"pageId":"6f1d2c3b-4a59-4e8d-9c7b-1a2b3c4d5e6f","patch":{"title":{"en-US":"Studio and team","it":"Lo studio"},"slugs":{"it":"studio-e-squadra"},"status":"published"}}
```

## page.forkTemplate

Fork a theme template (`templateId`, one template.index lists) into an editable site page row, once per template: the answer is the fork's page, whose tree (the template's, same node ids) you then change with tree.commit. Every page of that template renders through the fork from then on. Page validation and ownership checks apply.

- permission `site.structure` (admin, workspace owner); class `transaction`; writes `pages`; undoable with `history.undo`.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `templateId` | string (min 1) | yes |

Output: { page: { slug: string (min 1), slugs?: Record<string, string>, title: Record<string, string>, frame: string, dynamic: boolean, position: integer ≥-9007199254740991, parentId: string \| null, requireAuth: boolean, requiredRoles?: string (max 40)[] (≤50), meta: Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (… \| … \| …… (full schema: discover_operations)

Example input:

```json
{"templateId":"page"}
```

## page.setPassword

Protect a page with a password, change it, or remove it with `password: null`. A visitor sees the password form instead of the page until they enter it; members are asked too. The password is stored hashed and never answered: page answers say only `passwordProtected`. Like the other page fields it reaches the public site with the next publish. Run it alone in a batch: the input is redacted from the history and the audit log, and the change is not undone.

- permission `site.edit` (admin, editor); class `transaction`; writes `pages`; **not undoable**: alone in its batch.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `pageId` | string (min 1) | yes |
| `password` | string (min 4, max 200) \| null | yes |

Output: { page: { slug: string (min 1), slugs?: Record<string, string>, title: Record<string, string>, frame: string, dynamic: boolean, position: integer ≥-9007199254740991, parentId: string \| null, requireAuth: boolean, requiredRoles?: string (max 40)[] (≤50), meta: Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (… \| … \| …… (full schema: discover_operations)

Example input:

```json
{"pageId":"6f1d2c3b-4a59-4e8d-9c7b-1a2b3c4d5e6f","password":"press-preview-2026"}
```

## tree.node

Read one node of a page's draft tree with its props, styles, meta, variant and theme, and its children down to `depth` levels (1 by default, 0 for the node alone), without reading the whole tree. `path` names its ancestors from the root; `cut` lists the child ids left out at the depth limit. Find node ids in the page's outline resource; the answer's `revision` is the tree:<pageId> base revision of the batch that changes it.

- permission `site.read` (admin, editor); class `read`; writes nothing.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `pageId` | string (min 1) | yes |
| `nodeId` | nodeId | yes |
| `depth` | integer ≥0 ≤4 |  |

Output: { pageId: string, revision: integer ≥0, path: ({ id: nodeId, kind: "root" \| "section" \| "repeater" \| "outlet" \| "primitive" \| "component" \| "instance", type: string })[], node: { meta?: { canvas?: boolean, attributes?: Record<string, string>, reveal?: { effect: …, distance?: …, mode?: …, once: …, threshold: …, duration… (full schema: discover_operations)

Example input:

```json
{"pageId":"6f1d2c3b-4a59-4e8d-9c7b-1a2b3c4d5e6f","nodeId":"claim001","depth":1}
```

> The read to use before any node edit: props, styles, meta, variant and theme of one node, its children to `depth`. Its `revision` is the `tree:<pageId>` base revision. `cut` names the children left out: read them with another `tree.node` if you need them.

## catalog.index

List every node type this site can place, one entry each: its id (the node type of tree.commit inserts), kind, label, category, parts, states, slot names, what its children may be (`accepts`) and where it may sit (`parentOneOf`). Read one type's props schema with catalog.entry; list the presets with preset.index.

- permission `site.read` (admin, editor); class `read`; writes nothing.
- Input: `{}`.

Output: { theme: string, entries: { id: string, kind: string, label: string, category?: string, parts: string[], states: string[], slots: string[], accepts?: string[], parentOneOf?: string[] }[] }

Example input:

```json
{}
```

## catalog.entry

Read one node type's whole registry entry by its id (`box`, `ds.button`, `sticky-bar`): its props schema with each field's help, parts, states, slots and content model. Refused with 404 type_not_found for an id catalog.index does not list. Read `embed` before placing a map or a third-party video: its `loading` prop (`immediate`, `onClick`, `afterConsent`) keeps the iframe out of the page, behind a placeholder with a notice, a load button and an optional link (`notice`, `loadLabel`, `allowLabel`, `linkUrl`, `linkLabel`), until the visitor clicks or grants the external media consent.

- permission `site.read` (admin, editor); class `read`; writes nothing.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | string (min 1) | yes |

Output: { id: string, kind: "primitive" \| "ds" \| "behaviour" \| "section", label: string (min 1, max 80), keywords?: string (min 1, max 40)[] (≤16), category?: string, tags?: string[], propsSchema: ({ id: string, type: "text" \| "richtext-single" \| "richtext-inline" \| "richtext-block" \| "select" \| "toggle" \| "number" \| "range" \|… (full schema: discover_operations)

Example input:

```json
{"type":"ds.button"}
```
